units.title: Epidemiology of Acute Leukemia, Myeloid Precursor Lineages & AML Pathogenesis
units.sec: Epidemiology of Acute Leukemia, Myeloid Precursor Lineages & AML Pathogenesis
units.guide:
Leukemia distribution: Adults → 80% AML, 20% ALL; Children/adolescents → 90% ALL, 10% AML; Myeloid precursor stem cell → Myeloblast (granulocyte), Monoblast (monocyte), RBC, Platelets.
AML pathogenesis: (1) Clonal proliferation of myeloid precursors — Myeloblast (m/c) → myeloblastic leukemia (70–80%), Monoblast → monoblastic/myelomonocytic leukemia, RBC precursor → erythro-leukemia, Platelet precursor → megakaryocytic leukemia.
(2) Complete arrest of differentiation (myeloblast takes over marrow): high turnover → short history (2–3 months), acute presentation without CNS/testes/organ (spleen/liver/lymph nodes) involvement, pancytopenia manifesting as bleeding; marrow replacement → blood blasts → ↑↑ counts (poor prognosis) → late CNS involvement.

units.title: Hyperviscosity Note, 5-Point Hematological Diagnosis, AML Definition, Survival & Hereditary Risk Factors
units.sec: Hyperviscosity Note, 5-Point Hematological Diagnosis, AML Definition, Survival & Hereditary Risk Factors
units.guide:
Hyperviscosity: absent in AML, present in CML. 5-point diagnosis: 1. Morphology (bone marrow/blood cells), 2. Cytology/Cytochemistry (MPO/Sudan black), 3. Immunophenotyping by flow cytometry (CD markers), 4. Cytogenetics (recurrent genetic abnormalities), 5. Molecular genetics (inversion/deletion).
Definition: generalised neoplastic (clonal) proliferation of immature leucocytes ± blood/non-hematopoietic tissues; Leukemia = clonal WBC-lineage proliferation in marrow/blood; m/c cell = myeloblast; median age 65 yrs (seen in all ages); M > F.
5-year survival: >75 yrs almost NIL, >50 yrs ~20% with transplant. Notes: chronic disorders = mature cells; lymphoma = lymph node proliferation. Hereditary risk factors: defective DNA repair (Bloom, ataxia-telangiectasia), Diamond-Blackfan (inherited PRCA), inherited aplastic anemia (Fanconi, dyskeratosis congenita, Shwachman-Diamond).

units.title: AML Risk Factors: Germline/Syndromic Predisposition, Down Syndrome, Environmental & Hematological Diseases
units.sec: AML Risk Factors: Germline/Syndromic Predisposition, Down Syndrome, Environmental & Hematological Diseases
units.guide:
Hereditary continued: germline susceptibility (very minimal familial inheritance: germline CEBPA, germline GATA2), Kostmann syndrome (congenital agranulocytosis), Noonan syndrome.
Down syndrome: (a) Transient abnormal myelopoiesis — m/c hematological abnormality, seen at birth, resolves spontaneously in 2–3 months, d/t GATA-1 mutation; (b) AML — in 20%, within 4 years of age, megakaryocytic (M7) subtype, better prognosis than in a normal child.
Environmental: radiation, benzene, smoking, drug-induced (alkylating agents after 5–6 yrs; topoisomerase II inhibitors after 1–3 yrs: etoposide). Hematological: MPNs (PCV, PMF, ET, CML), PNH, aplastic anemia (eosinophilic fasciitis), myeloma, 25% of MDS (10–19% blasts) → AML (20% blasts).

units.title: Classification of AML: FAB Subtypes, WHO (2016) & WHO-5 (2023) Categories, and Recurrent Genetic Abnormalities
units.sec: Classification of AML: FAB Subtypes, WHO (2016) & WHO-5 (2023) Categories, and Recurrent Genetic Abnormalities
units.guide:
FAB classification (does not give prognosis): M2 myeloblast, M3 promyelocyte, M4 myelomonocyte, M5 monocyte, M6 erythroid, M7 megakaryocyte.
WHO (2016): AML with recurrent genetic abnormalities (blasts ≥20%), AML–MDS related & AML–therapy related (M6) [both poor prognosis], AML–NOS (M2, M3, M4), myeloid sarcoma. Recurrent genetic abnormalities (blasts ≥20% not required): good prognosis = t(15;17)/t(PML;RARα) [APML], t(8;21)/t(RUNX1;RUNX1 as printed), t(16;16)/inv(16) [CBFβ], NPM-1, CEBPA; bad = t(BCR;ABL)/t(9;22); very bad = FLT3-ITD.
WHO-5 (2023): 1. AML with recurrent genetic abnormalities (blasts ≥20% not required except CEBPA and t(BCR,ABL)), 2. AML–MDS, 3. AML–therapy related, 4. AML defined by differentiation (FAB). ICC classification: not used now.

units.title: Clinical Features of AML: Presenting Pancytopenia, Infections Note & Myeloid Sarcoma (Chloroma)
units.sec: Clinical Features of AML: Presenting Pancytopenia, Infections Note & Myeloid Sarcoma (Chloroma)
units.guide:
Presenting features: acute presentation (3-month history); pancytopenia → m/c complication is abnormal bleeding d/t prominent thrombocytopenia (bruising, petechiae, epistaxis, gingival bleeds, excess menstrual bleeding) and anemia (pallor, fatigue, weakness, palpitation).
ANC is normal → only minor infection/pustules; no fever (no cytokine production)/lymphadenopathy; no hepatosplenomegaly; bone pains rare (m/c in ALL); life-threatening hemorrhage in APML; meningeal/cardiac/urogenital rare. Note: complex infections in aplastic anemia (profound neutropenia) and hairy cell leukemia (neutropenia, monocytopenia).
Myeloid sarcoma/Chloroma: d/t extramedullary blast proliferation, uncommon, m/c site orbit, can occur independent of marrow involvement, associated with t(8;21), also in children; m/c cells myeloblast/monoblast (M4/M5) infiltrate gingiva (gum hypertrophy/gingivitis), liver, spleen, dental abscess, proctitis.

units.title: Skin Involvement (Leukemia Cutis vs Sweet Syndrome), Blood Picture & Myeloblast vs Promyelocyte Morphology
units.sec: Skin Involvement (Leukemia Cutis vs Sweet Syndrome), Blood Picture & Myeloblast vs Promyelocyte Morphology
units.guide:
Skin involvement: Leukemia cutis (non-tender violaceous nodular lesions on extensor forearms; M4/M5 AML; Rx chemotherapy) vs Sweet syndrome (tender erythematous/violaceous papules/plaques with dermal neutrophilic infiltration + fever on face, neck; AML, post G-CSF, PMF; Rx steroids).
Blood picture: normocytic normochromic anemia, platelets ↓↓ (<1 lac cells), total WBC count <4000 cells.
Morphology: Myeloblast (large uniform blast, high N:C ratio, pale blue scanty cytoplasm + granules, 1–4 prominent nucleoli, Auer rods ⊕ M3 > M2, fine dispersed chromatin) vs Promyelocyte (larger cell, more visible granules, nucleoli absent, clustering of Auer rods = faggot cells, M3/promyelocytic leukemia).

units.title: AML Cytology Stains, Immunophenotyping CD Markers, Cytogenetics, Molecular Mutations & European Risk Stratification
units.sec: AML Cytology Stains, Immunophenotyping CD Markers, Cytogenetics, Molecular Mutations & European Risk Stratification
units.guide:
Cytology: MPO (+), Sudan black (+), NSE (M4, M5, M7), PAS (M6, M7). Immunophenotyping: Myeloblast (CD11b, CD13, CD33, CD117, HLA-DR), Promyelocyte (CD13, CD33), Myelomonoblast (+CD14), Monoblast (+CD11c), Erythroid (glycophorin, spectrin), Megakaryocytic M7 (CD41, CD61).
Cytogenetics & mutations: t(8;21) RUNX1–RUNX1T1 (m/c, children, chloroma, M2, CD19+, good prognosis); t(16;16)/inv(16) (abnormal eosinophils = AML M4 Eo, organ infiltration, good prognosis); t(9;22) bad prognosis (except CML); c-Kit (in t(8;21)/t(16;16), bad prognosis); NPM1 (cup-shape blasts, good prognosis, m/c gene mutated); CEBPA (good prognosis, requires >20% blasts); FLT3-ITD (bad prognosis).
European risk stratification: Favourable = t(8;21), t(16;16), NPM1 without FLT3-ITD, CEBPA; Intermediate = no cytogenetic abnormalities; Unfavourable = all other mutations.

units.title: Bad Prognostic Factors, Treatment Risk Groups, 7+3 Induction Regimen, Post-Induction Care & Targeted Agents
units.sec: Bad Prognostic Factors, Treatment Risk Groups, 7+3 Induction Regimen, Post-Induction Care & Targeted Agents
units.guide:
Bad prognostic factors: elderly age, high presenting WBC count, cytopenias (anemia, leucopenia, thrombocytopenia) >1 month before diagnosis, therapy-associated AML, MDS-associated AML, chromosomal translocations.
Treatment risk groups: Standard = t(8;21), t(16;16), age <60 yrs, NPM1, CEBPA; High = all other cases. Induction (7+3 regimen, 2 cycles): Cytarabine 7 days continuous low-dose infusion + Daunorubicin I.V 3 days low dose (ECHO prior d/t cardiotoxicity).
Post-treatment: marrow takes 10–14 days to regenerate → high infection risk (catheters, gut flora) → mortality; start antibiotics at first sign (tachycardia/tremors/fasciculations). Targeted: Midostaurin (oral FLT3-ITD inhibitor if FLT3-ITD+), Oral venetoclax (BCL-2 inhibitor, promotes apoptosis).

units.title: Post-Induction Bone Marrow & MRD Evaluation, Consolidation Phase, Regimens in Unfit/Elderly, New Drugs & APML Intro
units.sec: Post-Induction Bone Marrow & MRD Evaluation, Consolidation Phase, Regimens in Unfit/Elderly, New Drugs & APML Intro
units.guide:
Evaluation after 2 induction cycles: Blast % (<5% → hematological remission, risk of relapse +; >5% → refractory AML, inevitable death) and MRD (<0.01% blasts in marrow → MRD– → consolidation; >0.01% → MRD+ → bad prognosis).
Consolidation: 1. Allogenic HSCT (indication: MRD–); 2. High-dose cytarabine (indication: standard risk with MRD–; transplant not mandatory). Unfit/elderly for 7+3: hypomethylating agents (azacitidine, decitabine) + venetoclax (BCL-2 inhibitor).
New drugs: Gemtuzumab–Ozogamicin (anti-CD33), Ivosidenib (IDH inhibitor). APML (AML M3) intro: young patient with bleeding & pancytopenia, t(15;17)/t(PML;RARα), good prognosis with treatment, smear shows hypergranular myeloblasts (as printed).

units.title: APML (AML M3): DIC Pathogenesis, Hypergranular vs Hypogranular Types, Sanz Criteria & Differentiation Syndrome
units.sec: APML (AML M3): DIC Pathogenesis, Hypergranular vs Hypogranular Types, Sanz Criteria & Differentiation Syndrome
units.guide:
Pathogenesis: promyelocyte granules contain thromboplastin → activates extrinsic cascade → DIC → early mortality from severe hemorrhage (medical emergency). Note: cells abundant in marrow but few in blood; start ATRA early if suspected; ↑ TF expression.
Types: Hypergranular (2/3, low WBC, faggot cells +, dark large granules, dumbbell-shaped bilobed nucleus) vs Hypogranular (1/3, high WBC, faggot cells –, few granules, butterfly-shaped bilobed nucleus).
Sans (Sanz) risk criteria: Low risk (WBC <10,000, platelets >40,000 → ATRA + arsenic trioxide, good prognosis) vs High risk (WBC >10,000, platelets <40,000 → ATRA + arsenic trioxide + idarubicin). APML differentiation syndrome (10 days post therapy): rapid count rise, fever, edema, pleural effusion, weight gain, lung infiltrates/dyspnea d/t cell adhesion to vascular epithelium & cytokine release; Rx I.V dexamethasone.
